title: In 2 Peter 1 What Does It Mean To Have Like Precious Faith With Other Believers
paragraphs: Understanding "Like Precious Faith" in 2 Peter 1

The opening of 2 Peter 1 is a profound passage that introduces us to the concept of "like precious faith." The apostle Peter addresses his letter to those "that have obtained a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and the Savior Jesus Christ" (2 Peter 1:1 ASV). This phrase is packed with theological significance and rich encouragement for all believers. Let’s explore what it means and why it matters.
1. The Meaning of "Like Precious Faith"

The phrase "like precious faith" (Greek: isotimos pistis) literally means "equally valuable faith" or "faith of the same kind." Peter is highlighting that all believers, regardless of background or status, share the same faith—a faith that is equally precious and valuable in God’s sight.
Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and the Savior Jesus Christ. - 2 Peter 1:1 ASV

This faith is not based on personal merit or heritage but is received as a gift through the righteousness of Jesus Christ. Peter, a Jewish apostle, places himself on equal footing with Gentile believers, emphasizing the unity and equality of all who trust in Christ.
2. The Source of This Faith

Peter makes it clear that this faith is "obtained" (or "received")—not achieved by human effort, but given by God’s grace. It comes "in the righteousness of our God and the Savior Jesus Christ." In other words, our standing before God is grounded in Christ's finished work, not our own righteousness.
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
This aligns with the biblical teaching that salvation is by grace through faith alone, and that the faith we possess is itself a precious gift from God.
3. The Unity of Believers

Peter’s language emphasizes the unity of believers. There are no "first-class" or "second-class" Christians. Whether apostles or new converts, Jews or Gentiles, all who believe in Christ share the same precious faith and standing before God.
There can be neither Jew nor Greek, there can be neither bond nor free, there can be no male and female; for ye all are one man in Christ Jesus. - Galatians 3:28 ASV

This powerful truth should foster humility and unity within the church. It also provides assurance: you do not need to envy the faith of others or doubt your own salvation if you are trusting in Christ.
4. The Goal and Growth of Precious Faith

Peter continues by urging believers to build upon this foundation of faith. He exhorts them to add to their faith virtue, knowledge, self-control, and other qualities that reflect spiritual maturity (2 Peter 1:5-7 ASV). This growth is not a means to earn salvation, but the fruit of the faith we already share.
Yea, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply virtue; and in your virtue knowledge... - 2 Peter 1:5 ASV
The call is to live out the implications of our shared faith, demonstrating godliness and love in our lives as evidence of genuine transformation.
5. Confidence and Assurance

Peter assures believers that living out this faith confirms their calling and election, providing stability and confidence in their relationship with God (2 Peter 1:10 ASV). Our assurance is rooted in the objective work of Christ and is demonstrated as we grow in grace.
Conclusion

To have "like precious faith" means to share in the same saving faith as all believers—faith that is a gift from God, rooted in Christ’s righteousness, and equally accessible to all. This truth unites believers, transcends backgrounds, and calls us to grow together in spiritual maturity. It is a source of profound assurance and a call to live out our faith in love and holiness.
